title: Seal the tomb (Matthew 27:57–66)
hookLine: a kindness nobody can pay back, and a stone the powerful make as sure as they can
carry: make it as sure as you can
tomorrow: the stone is sealed and guarded. so who's sitting on it?
last: TRULY THIS WAS THE SON OF GOD.

lines: SOME FAVORS CAN'T BE PAID BACK.
cards: Some favors can be paid back: a ride, a loan, a borrowed charger. Some never can. When the even was come, a rich man of Arimathaea named Joseph, also a disciple, goes to Pilate and asks for the body of Jesus.
He wraps it in clean linen and lays it in his own new tomb, cut out of the rock. He rolls a great stone to the door, and goes.
Two women stay: "And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre."

teach.h: WHAT DO YOU OWE THE DEAD?
teach.b: Here's the question underneath: what do you owe someone who can never pay you back? Matthew's answer is Joseph: his own tomb, clean linen, a great stone, and no thanks possible.
Now a neighbor, and this one is close to home. Joseph is doing what his own scripture asked. The Torah says a body hanged on a tree must not stay there through the night; bury it the same day.
And Jewish tradition has a name for this work.

When Jacob asks his son to deal kindly and truly with him and bury him, the teacher Rashi explains that kindness to the dead is chesed shel emet, true kindness, because the one you help can never repay you.
So Christians and Jews share this: burying the dead is love with no return address.
The honest difference: Matthew tells this burial as a pause before the third day, and Christians read it toward Easter; Judaism does not share that belief about Jesus. Then the next day.

teach.h: AFTER THREE DAYS I WILL RISE.
teach.b: The chief priests and Pharisees remember Jesus said, "After three days I will rise again," and ask for the tomb to be secured. Pilate: "Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can."

teach.h: SEALING THE STONE, SETTING A WATCH.
teach.b: "So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch."

teach.h: MAKE IT AS SURE AS YOU CAN.
teach.b: They already have what they wanted, and still can't rest without a stone, a seal and soldiers.

how: Some churches keep Holy Saturday, the day between Good Friday and Easter, as a quiet day of waiting at the tomb; in Jewish communities, caring for and burying the dead is honored as a kindness that cannot be repaid.

o: the scroll of the law sealed until a feast day
the Temple doors locked at night by the priests
the stone sealed and guarded by order of the powerful

games.q: seal the tomb — tap the pairs.
p: sealing the stone, setting a watch

s: Jesus was laid in a borrowed tomb that belonged to a stranger
Matthew says Joseph laid him in his own new tomb, hewn out in the rock.
Pilate told them to make the tomb as sure as they could
"Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can."
Jewish tradition calls kindness to the dead true kindness
Rashi on Genesis 47:29: chesed shel emet, because the dead can't repay it.

games.q: a company keeps deleting honest reviews of its product and hires more moderators to watch the comments. by Matthew 27:62–66, what does all that effort show?
o: they're afraid of a story they can't control.
the reviews must have been false all along.
they're simply being careful and thorough.
games.why: the powerful already had what they asked for, and still needed a stone, a seal and soldiers. a seal says two things: this is closed, and we closed it.

practice: Count on your fingers the people who did something for you that you can never pay back: someone who has died, a teacher long gone, a stranger who helped and left. Let each finger fold down slowly with a name or a face.
If you run out of fingers, start again.

wordCard.voice: Seal the tomb. A great stone, a seal on it, and soldiers set to make it as sure as anyone could.

orig.note: Greek: sealing; how they made the stone sure in Matthew 27:66.

carryVoice: Your line: make it as sure as you can, Pilate's words over a sealed stone. Rest well tonight.
